// diagnostic

E0227

A function whose parameter is marked `&` or `&&` is used as a value where the expected function type doesn't mark that parameter the same way, or a function value writes a parameter its slot reads (or reads one the slot writes).

What

A function whose parameter is marked `&` or `&&` is used as a value where the expected function type doesn't mark that parameter the same way, or a function value writes a parameter its slot reads (or reads one the slot writes).

Why

A function type gives each parameter plain read access unless it marks a write (`fn(&T)`) or a take (`fn(&&T)`), and a call through it passes each argument that way, so a value whose parameter access differs would lose or invent the write or take its parameter declares.

Fix

Call the function directly, mark the parameter in the function type the way the function does (`fn(&T)`, `fn(&&T)`), or pass a lambda that makes that call.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0227: tests/ui/enum_constructor_value_take.stderr.

Error [jet.MarkedFunctionValue]: `Sink.Out` can't be used as a function value here because it takes its payload (`&&FileWriter`)
  --> tests/ui/enum_constructor_value_take.jet:12:24
    |
 12 | run: fn() { print(wrap(Sink.Out)) }
    |                        ^^^^^^^^
 Why: `FileWriter` can't be copied out of a read parameter into the variant, so the constructor takes it, and a function type gives each parameter plain read access unless it marks a take (`fn(&&T)`)
 Fix: Mark the parameter in the function type (`fn(&&FileWriter)`), or build the case directly with `Sink.Out(…)`
